title: Scalar pullback and tensor coefficient square
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $t:Y\to X$ with $t\circ f=g$ in diagrammatic order, and $F,G$ arbitrary $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Write $S_f$ for restriction to scalar sheaves, $T$ for inverse image of scalar sheaves, $j_F:TS_fF\to S_gt^*F$ for scalarPullbackCoefficient, and $\mu_f:S_fF\otimes_k S_fG\to S_f(F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}G)$ for scalarTensorCoefficient [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations]. Let $\tau:t^*(F\otimes G)\to t^*F\otimes t^*G$ be the normalized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor]. For the oplax comparison $\delta$ obtained from the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction, the equality of scalar sheaf morphisms $T(\mu_f)\circ j_{F\otimes G}\circ S_g(\tau)=\delta_{S_fF,S_fG}\circ(j_F\otimes_k j_G)\circ\mu_g$ holds, in diagrammatic order. It contains no Ext classes or cohomology degrees.

source.place: Cohomology Tag 01F7; Modules Tag 01CD, normalized tensor pullback section identity. Official text read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01F7 and the indicated tag pages.

proof.text: Apply the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction to the two morphisms. Precompose their underlying presheaf morphisms with the tensorator of the sheaf inclusion. Evaluate over each open U on a pure tensor s tensor r. The defining adjunction identity for scalarPullbackCoefficient identifies each factor with the normalized module pullback unit applied to s or r. The section formula for scalarTensorCoefficient sends a pure tensor to tmulSection s r. The section normalization of module_pullback_tensor sends the unit applied to this tensor section to the tensor of the two unit sections. The oplax comparison is the mate of the lax tensor comparison for direct image, so its adjoint gives precisely the same tensor of unit sections. Thus both composites agree on pure tensors. The linear tensor universal property extends the equality to presheaf tensors, and the sheafification adjunction extends it to the sheaf tensor. Finally injectivity of the inverse-image adjunction gives the displayed coefficient square. Empty schemes and zero modules require no exception: all these section identities hold.
